Description
The Biology Department at East Tennessee State University (ETSU) is seeking a motivated masters student starting fall 2027 to join Dr. Ryan Stephens' lab (https://ryanbstephens.wordpress.com). The Stephens’ lab focuses on understanding ecological interactions and community dynamics with a strong focus on trophic ecology of mammals and their consumption and dispersal of fungal spores and seeds. Graduate students will have the opportunity to work on projects involving both field research and lab-based studies, contributing to our understanding of ecological interactions and the functional roles that small mammals play in forested ecosystems. There is room for project development depending on the student’s interest with main research foci including 1) truffle-mammal interactions and the dispersal of fungal spores, 2) seed selection and dispersal by small mammals, and 3) trophic niche dynamics of small mammals.
 Position Requirements:
A bachelor’s degree in biology, ecology, environmental science, or a related field.
Previous research experience in ecology, natural resources, biology, or a related discipline is preferred.
·       Experience with field data collection, especially small mammal live trapping or taking forest compositional measurements is preferred but not required.
A valid US drivers license (or the ability to get one).
 Opportunities and Support:
The position is based at ETSU in Johnson City Tennessee and is available beginning August 2027. The ideal candidate will be able to start field data collection in May of 2027. Field work will take place in the Blue Ridge Mountains of East Tennessee. The Masters student will have support for 2 years including a tuition waver and stipend ($12,200) along with summer salary guaranteed in 2027.
 To apply, please email ([email removed]) your CV, statement of research interests (2 pages max), and contact information for three references. Include “Graduate student application” along with your last name in the email title. Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled. To receive full consideration please apply before November 20, 2026. Please refer to https://www.etsu.edu/cas/biology/academics/ms_bio.php for information about the Biology M.S. program.

Ryan Stephens

ARS Office/Lab and Location: A research opportunity is currently available with the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Research Service (ARS), located in Aberdeen, Idaho.

The Agricultural Research Service (ARS) is the U.S. Department of Agriculture's chief scientific in-house research agency with a mission to find solutions to agricultural problems that affect Americans every day from field to table. ARS will deliver cutting-edge, scientific tools and innovative solutions for American farmers, producers, industry, and communities to support the nourishment and well-being of all people; sustain our nation’s agroecosystems and natural resources; and ensure the economic competitiveness and excellence of our agriculture. The vision of the agency is to provide global leadership in agricultural discoveries through scientific excellence.

The research activities will integrate traditional breeding with molecular and genomics-based approaches. Researching in laboratory, greenhouse, and field settings, you will help with experimental design, implementation, data collection, and data analysis. Under the guidance of a mentor, you will be given the opportunity to participate in studies focused on barley bacterial leaf streak, Fusarium head blight (FHB) and/or oat stem and crown rust disease research. Learn how traditional breeding and molecular/genomics-based approaches are integrated to improve barley and oat productivity, quality, and disease resistance.
Gain experience conducting research in laboratory, greenhouse, and field settings, including experimental design, implementation, data collection, and analysis.
Develop knowledge of major cereal diseases, including barley bacterial leaf streak, Fusarium head blight, and oat stem and crown rust.
Build skills in gene mapping and molecular-marker development for disease-resistance traits.
Gain experience with genome-, gene-, and transcript-level sequence analysis, including gene-expression studies.
Learn to investigate plant disease-resistance mechanisms using molecular, physiological, and genetic approaches.
Develop skills in analyzing, summarizing, and communicating research findings through internal reports, external presentations, and peer-reviewed manuscripts.

Appointment Length: The appointment will initially be for one year, but may be renewed upon recommendation of ARS and is contingent on the availability of funds.

Level of Participation: The appointment is full time.

Citizenship Requirements: This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens only.

ORISE Information: This program, administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and ARS. Participants do not become employees of USDA, ARS, DOE or the program administrator, and there are no employment-related benefits. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Health insurance can be obtained through ORISE.

Experience with plant disease research, preferably in cereals.
Demonstrated skills in molecular marker development, gene mapping, and sequence analysis.

Description
One Ph.D. Graduate Research Assistantship is anticipated at South Dakota State University beginning on or before January 2027 (flexible), contingent on candidate availability. This position will support a collaborative research project with the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) Habitat and Population Evaluation Team (HAPET) to quantify the ecological value of small wetlands embedded in agricultural landscapes of the Prairie Pothole Region (PPR). Small wetlands comprise the majority of basins in the PPR and are central to conservation investments through programs, yet key uncertainties remain regarding their hydrology, disturbance, and functional importance to waterfowl and other wetland-dependent species. The successful candidate will serve as the primary coordinating scientist for an integrated research program that combines long-term datasets (e.g., Four Square Mile Waterfowl Breeding Survey), high-resolution remote sensing, and targeted field validation to address management-relevant questions at landscape to regional scales.
 The student will work closely with USFWS HAPET scientists and other partners to develop reproducible analytical workflows, conduct spatial and statistical modeling, and contribute to decision-support tools that inform wetland conservation prioritization. The position will include both computational and field components, including validation of remote sensing products and coordination of field data collection across the PPR.
 Qualifications: Applicants should have an M.S. degree in wildlife ecology, wetland ecology, natural resources, geospatial sciences, environmental science, or a closely related field. Exceptional candidates with a B.S. and strong quantitative skills may be considered.
 Competitive candidates will demonstrate:
1)      Background in wetland, waterfowl, or landscape ecology, emphasizing agrarian systems.
2)      Experience with geospatial data analysis (e.g., GIS, remote sensing, LiDAR, etc.).
3)      Quantitative skills (e.g., statistical modeling, programming in R or similar platforms).
4)      Ability to manage and integrate large, complex datasets.
5)      Experience or interest in applying machine learning or computer vision approaches.
6)      Capacity to coordinate fieldwork across large spatial extents.
 The position will involve interaction with federal and state agencies, NGOs, and private landowners; professionalism, strong communication skills, and the ability to work effectively and coordinate with diverse partners are essential.
 Support: The assistantship includes:
- Annual stipend (approx. $26,000–$29,000 depending on year of appointment).
- Full tuition remission.
- Support for research, travel, and professional development.

To apply, submit a single PDF containing:
1. Cover letter describing research interests, relevant experience, and career goals.
2. Curriculum Vitae.
3. Contact information for at least three references.
 Unofficial transcripts (and GRE scores, if available) may be included or requested later.
 Send application materials and inquiries to: Dr. Joshua D. Stafford ([email removed]). Review of applications will immediately and continue until the position is filled.

Description
The Scordato Lab at Cal Poly Pomona invites applications for a Master’s student to study avian ecology in a Southern California agroecosystem. The Scordato lab is part of the SPACES Institute, a NASA-funded initiative aimed at integrating remote sensing data into on-the-ground assessments of biodiversity and ecosystem services. The SPACES Institute includes faculty from Cal Poly Pomona, UC Santa Barbara, and the UC Agriculture and Natural Resources extension. We work closely with farmers and conservation non-profits throughout our study region with the overall aim of improving biodiversity in complex agricultural landscapes.
 We are recruiting a Master’s student to study how native plant restoration and landscape-level vegetation structure affect avian communities across spatial scales. There is broad scope for the student to develop independent lines of inquiry, but any project will involve point counts in the field and use of remote sensing products. The student will have access to >4 years of longitudinal data on bird community structure, data on arthropod communities, newly collected high-resolution lidar and hyperspectral data, as well as existing NASA remote sensing products. The Master’s student will be expected to work on all aspects of the research project, collaborate closely with other members of our interdisciplinary research team, and lead the preparation of at least one peer-reviewed manuscript. The student will have opportunities to identify their own professional development priorities to advance their chosen career path. This position is funded for two years with the possibility of a third year. The expected start date is Fall 2027.
 Required qualifications: 1) a Bachelor’s degree in biology, ecology, environmental science, wildlife biology, or similar field; 2) strong writing and quantitative skills; 3) a valid US driver’s license.
 Preferred qualifications (but do not hesitate to apply if you do not have these): 1) experience with avian point counts and/or strong identification skills for Southern California birds; 2) experience conducting field research, particularly in challenging conditions; 3) familiarity with R and/or Python; and/or 4) experience working with geospatial data.
 Competitive applicants will be flexible, positive, and communicative during challenging fieldwork; enjoy data analysis and writing; and be passionate about communicating science to broad audiences. Our work involves extensive public outreach, and there are many opportunities to develop blogs, reports, and other media for the farming community involved in this project.
 To learn more about Cal Poly Pomona and its Masters graduate program, visit https://www.cpp.edu/sci/biological-sciences/graduate-studies/about.shtml 
 Read more about the project here: https://www.scordatolab.com/ and the SPACES Institute here: https://www.spacesinstitute.org/
 Please reach out Liz Scordato at [email removed] with any questions. To apply, please send the following to [email removed] by November 13th.

CV with academic and professional experience 
The names and contact information for 2-3 references

Description

Graduate assistantship focused on population ecology of moose – we are seeking a highly motivated person to pursue a PhD degree in the Environmental and Life Sciences Graduate Program at Trent University in Peterborough, Ontario, Canada. The graduate student will join a large team implementing a field research project on the factors limiting and regulating moose populations in Ontario. The field project is a multi-year program that entails the GPS radio collaring of moose, American black bears, wolves and white-tailed deer to assess cause-specific mortality of moose and examine predator-prey dynamics. This project is entering its third year and has collected a large amount of data on moose vital rates and movements. We are seeking a student to focus their research on moose population dynamics and the drivers of variation in moose vital rates. Specific research questions will be determined collaboratively between the student and research team. The successful applicant will have considerable responsibility and freedom to formulate and address basic and applied research questions grounded in ecological theory. Field work will be highly varied and will include live trapping and deployment of collars on black bears, wolves and white-tailed deer and helicopter capture of adult and calf moose. Further, the project involves deployment of remotely triggered trail cameras, collection of non-invasive samples for black bear population estimation, vegetation surveys, hunter surveys, aerial population surveys and more. The student will be expected to conduct significant field work for their specific project AND assist in all field aspects of the broader project. The student will be co-supervised by Dr. Joe Northrup and Dr. Brent Patterson both of the Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources & Trent University. 

 

Requirements

M.Sc. degree in ecology, wildlife biology, or related field is desired, but exceptional past experience may be considered in place of a M.Sc. degree. Applicants must meet the minimum entrance requirements for the Environmental & Life Sciences graduate program at Trent University.  Desired qualifications include a GPA >3.5 (4.0 scale). A strong background in ecology, demonstrated analytical capabilities, and passion for wildlife research are required. Strong quantitative, writing, and oral communication skills are also required. The strongest applicants will have demonstrated experience publishing in peer-reviewed journals, and with programming languages commonly used for statistical and scientific applications (e.g., R and Python), and familiarity with geospatial software (e.g., ArcMap, QGIS). Applicants should be physically fit, have significant field experience, be comfortable with flying in small planes and helicopters, and be capable of working in varied terrain for extensive periods in extreme conditions (e.g., temperatures that will range between 30 and -40 C, lots of biting insects etc.).

Application instructions

Initially, all applications are to be sent as follows. Please email a cover letter with an explicit statement of analytical/quantitative AND field experience and abilities, current CV, unofficial transcripts, scientific writing sample and contact info for ≥3 references as a single attachment to [email removed]. The successful applicant is expected to begin in spring or fall, 2027. Application deadline is November 15, 2026 but review of applications will begin immediately and continue until a suitable candidate is found. Once a successful applicant has been determined a formal application to the University is required, with a deadline of February 1, 2027.

 

Compensation

Students will receive a funding package of approximately $34,000 per year. This includes a combination of a graduate teaching assistantship, internal fellowships and a research assistantship. Further, during the first 2-3 years of the project, students working fulltime in the field will be provided shared housing. Tuition fees can be found here: https://www.trentu.ca/graduatestudies/financial-matters/student-account-and-tuition/research-and-thesis-based-program-fees. Numerous scholarships are also available and students are encouraged to apply (https://www.trentu.ca/graduatestudies/tuition-awards-funding/graduate-scholarships-and-awards). This funding package will not be reduced if a student is successful in obtaining a scholarship. 

Patterson and Northrup Labs

More information about the research groups of Drs. Brent Patterson and Joe Northrup can be found here: http://www.canidungulatelab.wixsite.com/brentpatterson and here: https://www.joenorthrup.com/. More information on the project can be found here: https://www.ontariomooseproject.ca/

We are excited to offer a unique research assistantship opportunity focused on advancing the understanding of white rhino behaviour and ecology in South Africa.
WildComm is dedicated to conserving biodiversity on private land by creating opportunities for research, education, and hands-on conservation action. Our mission is
to demonstrate that private land can deliver both ecological and economic value, supporting wildlife and ecosystems beyond traditional protected areas. By joining
WildComm, you’ll be part of a growing network of researchers, students, and conservationists working together to generate vital ecological data, inform evidence-
based management, and inspire new models for wildlife conservation.

The project addresses urgent questions about the long-term impacts of dehorning on rhino behaviour. Most existing research is short-term or limited in scale, leaving important gaps in our understanding of how dehorning affects rhino. Using behavioural observations, we collect long-term data from reserves with different
management strategies. By comparing behaviour, habitat use, and social structure, we aim to support evidence-based conservation decisions for this iconic and endangered species.

study:
Tracking and locating individual rhinos on foot using spoor and field signs
Conducting extended behavioural observation sessions from safe vantage points
Recording systematic scan samples and filming focal individuals
Coding and analysing behavioural footage using standardised ethograms

Moderate fitness level (endurance improves with experience)

Description
 Postdoctoral Researcher in Mountain Lion Population Genetics 
Nevada Cooperative Fish and Wildlife Research Unit & University of Nevada, Reno 
 Project description and responsibilities: We seek a Postdoctoral Researcher to lead a project quantifying mountain lion population genetic structure and landscape connectivity across Nevada. The postdoc will be based out of the Nevada Cooperative Fish and Wildlife Research Unit (NVCFWRU) in the Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Sciences (NRES) at the University of Nevada, Reno (UNR). Project objectives include estimating statewide population genetic diversity and differentiation, effective population sizes, and identifying the landscape drivers of genetic connectivity. The ideal candidate will have experience generating and analyzing genome-wide datasets and be able to develop/implement code (e.g. python, R) for raw data processing, estimating standard population genetic metrics, and integrating genomic data with spatial datasets. The postdoc will be expected to work closely with state agency staff, produce project reports, publish at least one peer-reviewed journal article, give presentations to cooperators and at professional conferences, and supervise project data management. 
The Postdoc will work on campus and be co-advised by Drs. Brian Folt and Marjorie Matocq. The Postdoc will be an integral part of our lab communities and will have opportunities to engage in mentoring, grant writing, developing research collaborations, and other aspects of professional development. Our lab communities are committed to the development of early-career scholars and we value intersectional diversity and work-life balance. 
 Qualifications: PhD in population genetics, wildlife biology, conservation biology, or a related field. Applicants must have experience in generating and analyzing genome-wide datasets (e.g. ddRAD or WGS) and conducting standard population genetic analyses. Candidates must have strong oral and written communication skills and must have strong data management skills. Preferred candidates will have knowledge of mammalian ecology and management, as well as a strong record of publishing peer-reviewed literature. 
 Salary and benefits: Annual salary of $62,500/year and full benefits for up to 18 months (or more, depending on funding). January 2027 start date preferred. 
 To apply: To apply, please email a letter of interest, CV, and contact information for 3 references to Folt and Matocq ([email removed], [email removed]). Interested applicants are welcomed to reach out to Folt and Matocq with questions via email before applying. We will begin reviewing applications on 26 Oct 2026 and the position will be opened until filled.
